chunks: Ali narrated from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Muhammad ibn Humran, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the testimony of a child. He said, 'It is only in the case of blood money (diyah); the first statement of the child is taken, and the second is not taken.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the testimony of a young child in Islamic law?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the evidentiary weight of a young child's testimony in homicide cases, a key topic in Shia fiqh regarding the reliability of witnesses. The ruling that only the first statement is binding reflects the scholarly principle of prioritizing initial, uncorrupted recollection over potential hesitation or alteration in subsequent utterances. This specific criterion ensures legal precision when applying blood money (diyah) to cases where adult testimony may be scarce.
